messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — embedding endpoint decisions for next quarter. Need clear defaults for batching, dims, response format, and launch criteria before roadmap freeze.
Arjun (Eng-Platform): +1. I have a proposal with tradeoffs. TL;DR: two-mode default (fast/default-cost vs high-precision).
Sam (Eng-ML): Explain the two modes?
Arjun (Eng-Platform): Mode A: low-latency default. 1k max items per request, 512 dims as default model (fast quantized). Aim: p95 latency <200ms for 16-item requests, throughput optimized. Mode B: high-precision. support up to 4096 dims, batch items up to 250, provide GPU-backed path, higher cost.
Liam (Solutions): Customers keep asking for single-request up to 10k items. Can we support that?
Arjun (Eng-Platform): 10k single-request pushes memory and scheduling. We could support chunking transparently: accept >max and internally shard into 1k chunks with reordering. That adds 10-20% latency and more tail variance.
Priya (SRE): Important: chunking increases resource fragmentation. For Dedicated/private we can offer larger single-shot windows, but hosted needs hard limits to keep SLOs. Also need per-tenant concurrency caps.
Jess (Customer Success): Major customers: RetailX wants 4096 dims and bulk export (5M vectors) for migrations. They asked SLA for throughput. They'd pay for Dedicated but want migration tooling.
Maya (PM): So action: default API should be safe for PLG (Mode A). Enterprise can opt into Mode B or Dedicated. Need launch criteria: 1) response shape final, 2) client libs updated, 3) perf guardrails and fallback, 4) migration guide for large dims.
Sam (Eng-ML): On model selection: recommend shipping with two verified models: rn50-512q (quantized, cheap) and rn-large-4096 (float16/8bit fallback). We should expose model aliasing like `r/rn-default` and `r/rn-precise-4096`. Registry needs metadata: dims, tokenization, typical latency at batch sizes.
Arjun (Eng-Platform): Response format options: Option 1: compact JSON arrays for each vector: `{ "id":"...", "vector": [f64,...] }`. Option 2: binary payload (base64) for vectors to save bandwidth + streaming chunk support. Which do we want as default?
Liam (Solutions): Bandwidth matters for customers doing millions of vectors. Binary base64 speeds things up but harder for quick debugging. Maybe default to JSON arrays for PLG and add `accept: application/x-embeddings-binary` header for advanced usage.
Priya (SRE): If we add binary streaming, we must add guards in the CDN/edge and enforce per-request size limits to avoid DoS. Also need per-request CPU budget for base64 decode.
Jess (Customer Success): Migration ask: add a `diff` mode that returns vecs + a small quality checksum so customers can verify their migrated vectors match within tolerance. Small feature but big for adoption.
Sam (Eng-ML): Suggest adding `quality_score` per vector (cosine vs baseline) as optional metadata when running Mode B. That ties to Redwood Optimize evaluations.
Maya (PM): Let's define concrete launch defaults: default_model = `r/rn-default` (512 dims), default_max_items = "1000", default_response = "json-array", default_timeout = "60s". Enterprise flags: enable_4096=true, max_items_enterprise=5000, allow_binary=true.
Arjun (Eng-Platform): SDKs: add streaming iterator for binary and json. Server-side: implement chunking and reassembly with preserved order + per-chunk retry. Also add `X-Embeddings-Request-Chunks` header for diagnostics.
Priya (SRE): SLAs: For PLG default: p95 <= 500ms for <=16 items, p99 <= 2s. For Dedicated with 4096: p95 <= 1s for 8 items, but call it best-effort. Need quota & alerting rules.
Liam (Solutions): Pricing implication: Mode B should be 3x token/unit baseline. Add note to pricing doc.
Jess (Customer Success): I'll draft the migration checklist: sample converter, chunker hints, SDK helpers, and `verify_diff` tooling.
Maya (PM): OK owners: Arjun -> infra & SDK changes. Sam -> model verification + quality metadata. Priya -> SLOs and quota enforcement. Jess -> migration docs + customer comms. Liam -> pricing grid. I'll own launch criteria + roadmap slot.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: feature/embeddings-batching-shim -> staging at 1918205600
Arjun (Eng-Platform): Quick ask: add API-level param `preferred_mode=[auto|fast|precise]` default `auto` (auto picks fast unless dims>512).
Sam (Eng-ML): Agree. Also add compatibility header `X-Embedding-Schema-Version: 1` so we can iterate response format without breaking clients.
Maya (PM): Good. Final checklist for roadmap sync: 1) Spec doc published (Arjun) 2) SDK PRs open (Arjun) 3) Model verification results (Sam) 4) SLOs + quotas defined (Priya) 5) Migration guide draft (Jess) 6) Pricing proposal (Liam). Target date: 2 weeks from now (1919410000).
Liam (Solutions): Noted. I'll surface any paying customers who want early access.
Jess (Customer Success): Adding RetailX as first pilot candidate.
Maya (PM): Thanks — will file RFC with these decisions after sync.
Arjun (Eng-Platform): I'll post the spec link once the PR lands."
